title: HIF-1alpha/LTBP2 axis activate HSCs to promote liver fibrosis by interacting with LOXL1 via the ERK pathway.
authors: Lu, Mengxin; Tao, Shuai; Zhao, Conglin; Wang, Neng; Hu, Qiankun; Li, Qiang; Qi, Xun; Li, Xinyan; Zhang, Yi; Tu, Chuantao; Huang, Yuxian; Chen, Liang
journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
one_liner_zh: 该文研究HIF-1alpha调控LTBP2并通过ERK通路与LOXL1互作促进肝星状细胞活化，虽含ChIP验证TF-DNA结合和分子对接，但核心是肝纤维化病理机制，非TF-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法研究。
abstract: Latent Transforming Growth Factor Beta Binding Protein 2 (LTBP2) is a multi-domain exocrine protein located in the extracellular matrix (ECM) and has been implicated in fibrosis across various organs. However, its role in liver fibrosis remains inadequately understood. This study aims to elucidate the function and mechanism of LTBP2 in hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) activation and liver fibrosis. Our findings indicate that LTBP2 expression is positively correlated with liver fibrosis and is significantly elevated in fibrotic liver tissues from both human and murine models. Importantly, AAV6-mediated knockdown of LTBP2 in HSCs markedly alleviates CCl4-induced liver fibrosis by inhibiting the HSCs activation and reducing collagen deposition in mice. Gain-of-function and loss-of-function experiments confirmed that overexpression or knockdown of LTBP2 can enhance or inhibit the activation of HSCs, proliferation, migration and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in LX-2 cells. Mechanistically, chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assays and dual-luciferase reporter gene assays revealed that Hypoxia-inducible Factor 1alpha (HIF-1alpha) promotes LTBP2 expression by directly binding to the LTBP2 promoter region. Furthermore, molecular docking and co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) experiments demonstrated an interaction between Lysyl Oxidase Like Protein 1 (LOXL1) and LTBP2. Rescue experiments verified that LTBP2 interacts with LOXL1 via the ERK signaling pathway to promote the activation of HSCs and EMT. Our results provide compelling evidence that the HIF-1alpha/LTBP2 axis facilitates the activation of HSCs and EMT by interacting with LOXL1 through ERK signaling pathway, suggesting that LTBP2 may serve as a potential therapeutic target for liver fibrosis.
abstract_zh: 潜在转化生长因子β结合蛋白2（LTBP2）是一种位于细胞外基质（ECM）中的多结构域外分泌蛋白，并已被涉及在多种器官的纤维化中。然而，其在肝纤维化中的作用仍未被充分理解。本研究旨在阐明LTBP2在肝星状细胞（HSCs）活化及肝纤维化中的功能与机制。我们的研究结果表明，LTBP2表达与肝纤维化呈正相关，并且在人类和小鼠模型的纤维化肝组织中显著升高。重要的是，通过AAV6介导的LTBP2敲低在HSCs中显著缓解了CCl4诱导的肝纤维化，其机制是抑制HSCs活化并减少小鼠中的胶原沉积。功能获得和功能丧失实验证实，LTBP2的过表达或敲低可增强或抑制LX-2细胞中HSCs的活化、增殖、迁移及上皮-间质转化（EMT）。在机制上，染色质免疫沉淀（ChIP）实验和双荧光素酶报告基因实验揭示，缺氧诱导因子1α（HIF-1α）通过直接结合LTBP2启动子区域促进LTBP2表达。此外，分子对接和免疫共沉淀（Co-IP）实验证明了赖氨酰氧化酶样蛋白1（LOXL1）与LTBP2之间的相互作用。拯救实验验证了LTBP2通过ERK信号通路与LOXL1相互作用，以促进HSCs的活化和EMT。我们的结果提供了有力证据，表明HIF-1α/LTBP2轴通过ERK信号通路与LOXL1相互作用促进HSCs的活化和EMT，提示LTBP2可能作为肝纤维化的潜在治疗靶点。
